newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND FIGHT BACK AGAINST ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND FIGHT BACK AGAINST ZIMBABWE.

text.p: England's batsmen fought back strongly on the fourth day of the second test against Zimbabwe at Harare Sports Club on Sunday.
Alec Stewart and Nick Knight put on 68 for the second wicket to cancel England's first innings deficit of 59 and at lunch the tourists were 79 for two, a lead of 20.
Resuming at 17 for one, Knight struggled against the new ball attack of Heath Streak and Eddo Brandes but Stewart was in good form from the start.

Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell shuffled his four-man pace attack in an effort to force a breakthrough but it was the introduction of Paul Strang's leg spin 20 minutes before lunch which produced the breakthrough.
The first ball of Strang's second over took the outside edge of Knight's bat and went via the wicket-keeper's pads to Campbell at first slip. Knight made 30 from 84 balls with three boundaries.
At lunch Stewart had reached 41 with Nasser Hussain on two.
